articles.title: From Ocean Trash to Pavement: Hawaii's Bold Experiment with Plastic Roads
articles.summary: Hawaii has hauled 90 tons of plastic marine debris from the Pacific and is testing it in asphalt roads. Researchers are investigating whether these roads shed microplastics—tiny toxic bits. It's the first state to use ocean plastic in pavement, a promising but tricky solution.

articles.title: Meet the Triassic Croc Relative That Masqueraded as an Ostrich Dinosaur
articles.summary: Labrujasuchus expectatus, a newly identified shuvosaur from Ghost Ranch, walked on two legs, had tiny forelimbs, and a toothless beak—yet it's a crocodile relative. The fossil fills a long-predicted evolutionary gap, showing how croc cousins experimented with dinosaur-like bodies.

articles.title: A Closed Hospital, a Fatal Heart Attack, and the Limits of a $50 Billion Rural Health Fund
articles.summary: Stanley Sears died after a heart attack in Martin County, N.C., a year after its only hospital closed. His sister wonders if he could have been saved. A $50 billion rural health fund is touted as a lifeline, but it can't reopen shuttered facilities like Martin General.
